optimizedContext.value:
# runIndexProjectGraph

## Rules

- `runIndexProjectGraph(ctx: SdkHostContext, input: RunIndexProjectGraphInput): Promise<RunIndexProjectGraphResult>` resolves config, target/all workspaces, project/graph/version/VCS inputs; invokes `IndexProjectGraph` on open provider.
- Explicit `input.provider` plus `input.beforeOpen` or `input.afterClose`: throw `InvalidProviderLifecycleError`. Explicit provider MUST be open; caller-owned: SDK MUST NOT close, recreate, retry. Forward `force` to `IndexProjectGraph`.
- No provider: use `withOpenGraphProvider(ctx, ..., { beforeOpen: input.beforeOpen, afterClose: input.afterClose })`.
- Transient recovery only when `input.force` and initial `open()` raises typed recoverable storage-open error: helper closes provider, calls `provider.recreate()`, retries `open()` plus indexing exactly once. Preserve hooks; cleanup once/provider lifetime.
- Rethrow non-recoverable/untyped open errors, recovery failure, second open failure; no deletion/retry.
- `acquireGraphIndexLock` MUST NOT run in orchestration. CLI MAY acquire via `beforeOpen`.
- Forward `input.onProgress` unchanged. `RunIndexProjectGraphResult` preserves `IndexProjectGraph` fields: counts, workspace breakdown, errors, full-rebuild result; no lossy mapping.

## Constraints

- SDK owns force-only typed-open recovery decision; Code Graph owns `recreate()` and closed-provider precondition.
- Normal reads/non-forced indexing surface original typed open failure.
- Caller owns explicit provider lifecycle; `withOpenGraphProvider` owns transient lifecycle.
